card.occupation: Senior technical sales executive for an industrial fixings and fasteners distributor based on a trading estate in Walsall. He covers key accounts across the Midlands and is out on the road three or four days a week, regularly working 50 to 55 hours.
card.education_detail: Left school in Walsall at 16 with a handful of O-level-equivalent GCSEs. Did a BTEC National in mechanical engineering at the local college while working as a stores lad at an engineering firm. Later picked up company-paid sales training and an IOSH Managing Safely certificate. No degree, and he likes pointing out he's never needed one.
card.household: Lives with his wife Karen (49, part-time receptionist at a dental practice) in a four-bed detached on a newish estate they moved to in 2016. Their son Liam (24) moved out last year and lives in Lichfield with his girlfriend. Their daughter Jade (21) is in her final year at Nottingham Trent and is home some weekends. There's a cockapoo called Bailey, who Karen mostly walks.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Walsall. His dad was a toolsetter and his mum worked in a school kitchen. Christened and married in the Church of England, and he ticks 'Christian' on forms, but he only goes to church for weddings, funerals and the odd carol service. He thinks of himself as working class done good and is quite proud of the move from a terrace in Bloxwich to a detached in Aldridge.
card.professional_persona: Confident, persuasive and very target-driven. He's good at reading what a buyer wants to hear and at keeping key contacts sweet with football tickets and lunches. He tends to round his numbers up and his problems down. He's been known to take a bit more credit for a won contract than he strictly earned, and he treats mileage and expenses as a perk to be optimised. Colleagues find him good company but don't fully trust him. He doesn't get rattled when a deal goes wrong, and he just moves on to the next one.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Walsall FC fan who goes to a few home games a season and follows the rest on the radio. He also likes being seen at Villa Park in corporate hospitality when a supplier pays. Plays golf most Sunday mornings at a members' club near Sutton Coldfield, off a handicap of around 16. He describes it as 'about 14 on a good day' and isn't above a generous lie in the rough.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. He watches whatever's on the telly with Karen: Gogglebox, Line of Duty repeats, Strictly results night. He likes the odd Jason Statham film. He's been to see Peter Kay and a couple of tribute acts at the Grand Theatre in Wolverhampton. Music is mostly 80s and 90s stuff in the car: Simply Red, UB40, Oasis.
card.travel_persona: Two holidays a year, usually all-inclusive in Spain, Tenerife or Turkey. He likes a 'proper hotel' with a decent pool and lets people know when they've got an upgrade. He did Dubai once for his 50th and still brings it up. He isn't interested in wandering round old towns or museums and prefers to stick with what he knows will be good.
card.culinary_persona: Meat and two veg, a Sunday roast, a curry from the local on a Friday, and a carvery at the Toby when they can't be bothered. He'll have a bacon bap from the van on the trading estate. Karen does most of the cooking. He 'does the barbecue' in summer, which means standing over it with a lager. He orders steak whenever he's out on a supplier's card.
hobbies_and_interests: Golf on Sundays with the same three mates
His car, a leased BMW 5 Series he keeps immaculately clean
Watching Sky Sports football and the darts
Pub quiz at the local once a month, mainly for the sport and general knowledge rounds
Keeping the front lawn and drive looking smarter than the neighbours'
skills: Product knowledge on industrial fixings, anchors and threaded products
Reading technical drawings and spec sheets at a practical level
Talking to just about anyone at a trade counter or a site office
card.career_goals: Wants to be made sales manager for the region before the current one retires, mainly for the bigger car allowance and the title. Failing that, he'd take a better-paid key account role with a competitor. He'd like to retire at 60 on a decent pension with the mortgage cleared, and he talks loosely about 'a place in Spain' without having looked into it properly.
card.voice: Relaxed, chatty and a bit salesy. He talks at a steady pace and speeds up when he's on a topic he likes, such as cars, golf or work wins. He has a light Walsall/Black Country accent rather than a broad one. He uses 'mate' a lot, says 'give it me' and 'bap' naturally, and sometimes says 'tara' at the end of a call. His fillers are mostly 'er' and the odd 'erm', with 'sort of' as his main hedge. He tags sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah?' when he wants agreement. He's comfortable with silence because it doesn't bother him, and he'll often fill it with an anecdote that makes him look good. He sometimes says 'sorry' to repair a line, as in 'sorry, what was the question again?'
card.typing: Quick and practical. He usually starts with a capital letter but doesn't always end with a full stop. Apostrophes are mostly there but he sometimes drops them ('dont', 'its'). He uses the odd 'tbh' and 'etc'. Answers are short and to the point. He might use 'lol' once, and he never uses emojis on a form. He occasionally typo-corrects and occasionally doesn't bother.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to, with a firm handshake energy even over video. He's quick to find common ground, usually football or holidays, and drops in markers of success like the car, the house or the golf club. He comes across as confident, slightly showy and fun. He's not someone who'd open up emotionally, and he gives smooth, polished answers rather than reflective ones.
small_things: How bad the M6 was around junction 10 this morning
Bailey the dog chewing a slipper
How much the curry house has put its prices up
The van on the trading estate doing a decent bacon bap
deeper_things: He's a bit worried his pension pot isn't as big as he lets on, though he'd frame it as 'keeping an eye on it' rather than admit to worry
His dad died of a heart attack at 64 and Gary has quietly started having his blood pressure checked
He was passed over for the sales manager job once before and still resents the bloke who got it
Things with Karen are steady but a bit flat since the kids left, and they don't do much together apart from holidays
He's prouder of Jade going to university than he usually says, being the first in the family
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen-diner table, camera angled slightly up at him. He's lit mainly by a large window off to his left, so the right side of his face is a little shadowed, with grey afternoon daylight. He has a broad, clean-shaven face with a slight tan and a confident half-smile. His hair is short, greying at the sides and thinning on top, with a bit of gel at the front. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip jumper with a small company logo on the chest and a white collar showing underneath, and no glasses. Behind him is a glossy grey kitchen with white quartz worktops, a Nespresso machine and a bowl of fruit. A large wall clock with Roman numerals hangs above a door to the hallway. On the island there's a set of BMW keys on a leather fob next to a phone face-down. Through the doorway a golf bag is just visible propped against the wall.
